question: Should `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` be accepted as a supported public subagent capability-policy API across Gateway and persisted child sessions, with CLI harnesses responsible for enforcement or fail-closed rejection?
rationale: This is an additive security-sensitive public tool and Gateway surface whose long-term semantics, especially for non-embedded harnesses and persisted sessions, require repository-owner intent beyond correcting the current documentation defect.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded capability
options.body: Keep the additive API, correct the CLI contract, and require current-head proof that unsupported CLI harnesses fail closed.

options.title: Limit the first release to embedded runs
options.body: Reject the field before CLI dispatch until each CLI harness has an explicit enforcement contract and proof.

options.title: Pause for a broader policy design
options.body: Defer the API until maintainers define a single cross-harness capability-policy contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded capability
recommendation.body: Keep the additive API, correct the CLI contract, and require current-head proof that unsupported CLI harnesses fail closed.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline routed the initial public-policy discussion to this repository decision-maker.
